# react-formkit

> React + TypeScript form component library built on React Hook Form and Zod. Fields are declared
> once - as JSX or as a plain data config - and the same pipeline derives the Zod schema, the
> required indicators, the validation messages and the rendered controls from that single
> declaration.

Version 0.2.1, MIT. Built against React 19, react-hook-form 7, @hookform/resolvers 5 and zod 3.
`react-select` and `react-phone-input-2` back the multiselect and phone controls, but the package
root imports both at the top level, so they have to be installed even by an app that uses neither.
Type declarations are not generated yet, so the published package ships without `.d.ts` files.

Two ways to build a form, sharing one runtime:

- **JSX**: `<Form validationSchema={schema}>` with `<FormField name type label />` children.
- **Config**: a `FormConfig` array plus `useFormFromConfig` and `<ConfigFields />`, which derives
  default values and a Zod schema from the data.

Everything is exported from the package root; there are no deep import paths.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): install, the control table, usage for both form styles, config-driven
  forms, conditional fields, theming via CSS custom properties, and the current known limitations.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how to make changes in this repository - required checks, where each
  kind of change belongs, and the constraints that are not visible from the call site.
- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): released versions.

## API surface

- [src/index.ts](src/index.ts): the public barrel; re-exports the five area barrels below.
- [src/form/index.ts](src/form/index.ts): `Form` (with a loading-aware submit button),
  `BasicForm` (same pipeline, bring your own submit control), `ButtonWithFormLoader`,
  `withSubmitButton`.
- [src/field/index.ts](src/field/index.ts): `FormField`, `Field`, `FieldMessage`,
  `ConditionalField`, `matchesCondition`, `FormFieldArray`.
- [src/controls/index.ts](src/controls/index.ts): `Control` (the type router) and every concrete
  input - text, numeric, textarea, select, checkbox, checkbox-group, radio, switch, password,
  email, url, date, time, datetime, multiselect, autocomplete, multi-autocomplete, phone.
- [src/validation/index.ts](src/validation/index.ts): validators (common, number, charset, name
  presets), `asyncCheck` for debounced remote rules with `useIsAsyncValidating` for its pending
  state, the message map, `useFormLevelValidators` for cross-field rules, `useIsFieldRequired`,
  `useFormConfig`, `ValidationSchemaContext`.
- [src/config/index.ts](src/config/index.ts): `FormConfig`, `FieldConfig`,
  `ValidationDescriptor`, `useFormFromConfig`, `buildSchema`, `ConfigFields`.

## Behaviour worth knowing before generating code

- [src/validation/messages.ts](src/validation/messages.ts): every built-in message lives in
  `defaultMessages`. `setMessages` replaces the app-wide map; the `messages` prop on
  `Form`/`BasicForm` overrides per form; `withMessages` performs the scoped swap underneath.
  **Messages resolve when the schema is built, not when the module loads** - validator factories
  run outside React, so React context cannot reach them. Parameterised messages are functions;
  overrides may be templates with named placeholders such as `{min}` so a JSON bundle can supply
  them.
- [src/form/Form.tsx](src/form/Form.tsx): `validationSchema` accepts `ZodSchema` **or**
  `() => ZodSchema`. Per-form `messages` only affect a builder, because a ready-made schema
  already carries its strings. `mode` is passed straight to React Hook Form.
- [src/validation/validators/async.validators.ts](src/validation/validators/async.validators.ts):
  `asyncCheck(base, check, options)` debounces a remote check onto a field. **Its debounce state
  lives in the closure the validator was built with**, so the schema has to be stable. A verdict
  about a value the field has moved on from never decides the current value, an empty value is
  never sent, and a check that throws fails open. Hand-written schemas only, not configs.
- [src/validation/useIsAsyncValidating.ts](src/validation/useIsAsyncValidating.ts):
  `useIsAsyncValidating(fieldName)` is true while that field waits on its remote check, and a burst
  of keystrokes is one wait rather than one per key. **Do not substitute React Hook Form's per-field
  `isValidating`** - under a resolver the parse is the whole schema, so RHF marks the field whose
  event started it and marks every mounted field on submit. Keep `asyncCheck` outermost: zod methods
  that clone rather than wrap, `.describe()` among them, detach the pending channel.
- [src/config/buildSchema.ts](src/config/buildSchema.ts): turns `ValidationDescriptor[]` into a
  Zod schema. An explicit `message` on a descriptor wins; otherwise the message map supplies the
  default. A `showWhen` field is validated only while its condition holds.
- [src/config/useFormFromConfig.ts](src/config/useFormFromConfig.ts): derives the defaults and the
  schema, **memoised on a signature of field names and types**, so an inline config array literal
  is not a performance problem. **The trap is the inverse: a `validation` entry, a `message` or a
  `defaultValue` changed without renaming or retyping its field does not reach the schema or the
  defaults**, and the form keeps validating against the first build. Adding, removing, renaming or
  retyping a field does refresh them. `label`, `placeholder`, `options`, `disabled` and `showWhen`
  are read fresh each render, because `fields` is the caller's own array handed back. A duplicate
  `name` throws during render - `useFormFromConfig: duplicate field name(s): <names>` - rather than
  letting the last field win in the defaults and the schema separately.
- [src/field/ConditionalField.tsx](src/field/ConditionalField.tsx): conditions are `is`, `isNot`
  or a `test` predicate. In a config, a hidden field's value is dropped; with the standalone
  component, clearing is opt-in via `clear`.
- [src/field/FormFieldArray.tsx](src/field/FormFieldArray.tsx): repeats its children once per item
  in an array-valued field, as a render prop. Build each field's name from the row's `name`
  (`contacts.0`) rather than composing the index. Rows are keyed by react-hook-form's row id, so a
  reorder moves a row. Each row also carries `remove`, `moveUp`, `moveDown` and `isFirst`/`isLast`;
  the array-level `actions` render prop supplies `append` and `count`, and renders in the empty
  state too so an emptied array can be refilled. A move past either end is refused rather than
  passed on. The markup is always the caller's - the component hands over callbacks, not buttons.
  Hand-written schemas only; a config cannot express a repeated field. `useIsAsyncValidating` takes
  a row's own field name, so a row with an `asyncCheck` on it has its own pending indicator.
- [src/validation/useIsFieldRequired.ts](src/validation/useIsFieldRequired.ts): the required
  indicator is inferred from the schema rather than declared on the field. The lookup walks a
  field PATH (`address.street`, `contacts.0.email`) via `fieldAt` in `schema.utils.ts`, unwrapping
  each container on the way down and leaving the field itself wrapped - whether it is optional is
  the question being asked. An array index is matched and discarded, since every element shares
  one schema.

## Optional

- [src/styles/theme.scss](src/styles/theme.scss): the CSS custom properties available for
  theming (`--fk-focus-color`, `--fk-border-color`, `--fk-focus-ring`, `--fk-disabled-bg`,
  `--fk-radius`).
- [tests](tests): vitest suites mirroring `src/` by area; the config and message suites are the
  clearest executable specification of the behaviour described above.
